We are extremely disappointed and deeply angry.

Our dog, who was a patient at this clinic, suddenly became very ill: he vomited several times, then froze, rolled onto his back, and barely moved. We immediately called the clinic, who asked us to have an emergency vet come to our home.

When his condition worsened, we called the clinic again, specifying that we could bring him in immediately. We were told there were no appointments available and that we would have to wait for the emergency vet.

We waited for almost four hours. Unfortunately, our dog died five minutes after the vet arrived.

And that is precisely what infuriates us: we are now convinced that our dog could perhaps have been saved if he had received treatment sooner. Unfortunately, we will never know what might have happened with immediate intervention, but we do know that when we called the clinic back, we indicated that his condition was extremely worrying and that we were ready to come immediately.

After his death, we called the clinic again to inform them and express our bewilderment. Instead of acknowledging our distress, the situation was dismissed, and we were told that we hadn't properly explained the situation and that it wasn't the person we had spoken to on the phone… A convenient way to pass the buck.

We're not claiming that they could necessarily guarantee his survival. However, we would have expected such an alarming situation to be taken seriously and urgently reassessed.

I sincerely hope, as I said on the phone, that in the future the clinic will take owners' calls more seriously when they report that their pet is in great distress. For us, we haven't simply lost a dog. We lost a member of our family, a brother, our baby.

He held a huge place in our lives, and his loss has devastated us.

Not to mention the images that haunt us today (his pain, his eyes, me having to perform CPR and mouth-to-mouth resuscitation)—you can imagine all that…

We trusted them to take care of him as we did ourselves. Today, that trust is shattered, and we will sadly always feel that he deserved to be cared for sooner.

Thank you to Dr. Julia Campo and the entire team for taking such good care of my Laska these past two years. Her guidance was invaluable and allowed Laska and me to find a peaceful end. I am extremely grateful, and I hope Laska is too.

Hello,

This morning I took my dachshund to the emergency room because he had swallowed a sock without me realizing it. I was immediately greeted by a young man who asked me for my personal information and that of my dog. He then escorted us upstairs, where we met veterinarian Laure Lustman.

The doctor examined my dog ​​with great care and recommended two remedies to monitor his health. With calm, professionalism, and expertise, she then managed to expel the sock. My dachshund is now doing great.

I want to compliment the entire staff for the prompt reception and care we received, and especially the doctor for her kindness, professionalism, and great expertise.

If you're a tourist and encounter a similar emergency, I strongly recommend contacting them.
Thank you so much, Ms. Thevenet! Looking forward to seeing Chateigne again ;)

I don't usually leave negative reviews, but my experience with this clinic compels me to do so.

My dog ​​suffered from elbow dysplasia with a bone fragment in the joint. Despite several consultations, the diagnosis wasn't made correctly, and he was repeatedly prescribed anti-inflammatories without any lasting improvement.

Several X-rays were taken. However, I was clearly told that these X-rays were either not interpreted or difficult to read. So, I have a simple question: why take X-rays if they can't be properly interpreted?

Subsequently, my dog ​​was referred for physiotherapy, even though a specialized FRÉGIS center confirmed that this wasn't appropriate and that I should consult an orthopedic surgeon.

It was ultimately thanks to this external recommendation that my dog ​​was able to have surgery, and today he's doing very well.

I want to make it clear that I strongly advise against Dr. Willms. I felt that the financial aspect took precedence over the quality of care, which is very regrettable when it comes to living beings.

I sincerely regret the lack of an accurate diagnosis and appropriate referral, which resulted in a significant waste of time and considerable expense.

I do not recommend this clinic.
Dr. Sebaali Richard

I wholeheartedly recommend this practice for the quality of care and attention given to both animals and their owners.

I would especially like to thank Dr. Willms and the entire veterinary assistant team for their support throughout my dog ​​Joy's illness, right up to the end. She loved coming to the practice, which is quite rare and deserves to be highlighted. She was always greeted with gentleness, care, and great kindness. I came with my girlfriend on March 24, 2026. We brought our cat Blanco in for an emergency.
Thank you to Elena, she was very professional and knew how to find the right treatment for our cat. Thank you again! 🙏 …

Our cat Saka passed away during the night of December 30th to 31st, 2025, while under the care of the Sevetys clinic in the 8th arrondissement of Paris:

We first went to the clinic on December 29th because our cat was experiencing a urinary obstruction. He was seen by a veterinarian who catheterized him to empty his bladder. The procedure went well, and we left reassured.

On the evening of December 30th, our cat was unfortunately unable to urinate again. We returned to the clinic for further examination. The on-call veterinarian informed us that another catheterization was necessary and took our cat in to perform the procedure. He then asked us to wait in the waiting room.

The minutes began to tick by, 10 minutes, then 20 minutes… without any news. The wait seemed increasingly unnaturally long, and our anxiety began to grow. We finally decided to go back to the operating room to find out what was happening.

Looking at our cat, I immediately had the impression he wasn't breathing. I was the one who alerted the vet, asking if he had checked his vital signs and if he was still breathing. The vet then asked me to leave the operating room and began CPR.

Five minutes later, he came to tell us that our Saka had died...

The next morning, during a call with the clinic manager, we were told that an error in the care had likely occurred.

Since then, despite several letters and a formal complaint filed on January 16th, we still haven't received a clear answer or explanation regarding the exact circumstances of his death.

Faced with this silence and complete lack of transparency, we were forced to file a complaint so that responsibility can be established.

Saka wasn't "just a cat." He was part of our family. Losing him under these circumstances is already extremely painful.

Receiving no explanation or response from the clinic is even more so.

Today, we are still waiting for answers.
Following a pulmonary edema requiring cardiac monitoring, our cat was very well treated there (no stress, detailed explanations etc...).

(Our cat had previously seen two inexperienced vets near our home, as our usual vets were on vacation, and they made a mistake.)

I agree with the comments about the decline of this clinic, which has become a machine for prescribing tests rather than prioritizing animal welfare. After treating my dog ​​and then my cat, who passed away at the age of 8 in January 2025, and after a battery of tests that led to two referrals to another clinic for scans and all sorts of comprehensive examinations, we were diagnosed with epilepsy six months before his death. He was given a heavy dose of (unnecessary) medication, but his respiratory problems were ignored. Despite the history of these tests and treatments, which were meticulously followed, six months after his death they didn't even bother to explain the cause of his passing. A kitten will be joining our family, but I will be changing veterinarians; it's impossible to trust them.

The prices are no longer affordable; in fact, they're exorbitant. I have five cats, and I can't afford to pay such sums for a vaccination and consultation—over 100 euros, the price of a consultation with a doctor, like a gynecologist. I'm sorry, but I've decided to go to another vet where the reception will be better and more pleasant. Taking the time with people is important, and reassuring them is our job. I've been a veterinary assistant for over 20 years. Best of luck, and if I ever meet Michael, I'll explain to him why I no longer come.

My little cat Mashka had been followed by this clinic for 18 years and I continued to trust them, wrongly.
Indeed, during the last visit on December 14th, my cat had lost a lot of weight. Dr. Campo's diagnosis: thyroid problem. She performed a blood test which confirmed it.
Unfortunately, she either didn't see or didn't want to tell me about a very high white blood cell count, which indicates a serious infection.
Mashka's health deteriorated rapidly in just a few days. I had to take her to the Maisons-Alfort Veterinary School on December 30th, where she was hospitalized. On December 31st, the vet told me there was nothing more that could be done, and I had to resign myself, with immense pain, to having her euthanized so she would stop suffering.
The La Boétie veterinary clinic charged me 360 ​​euros for a 10-minute visit and a blood test, asking me to bring her back in three months. I get the impression that for them, the longer the animal lives, the more they can charge without any concern for your little companion's pain. This is a far cry from Dr. Silberg's way of practicing. 18 years ago
This clinic has simply become a money-making machine.
